newsitem.title: FRANCE: French welfare body calls for CADES report.
newsitem.headline: French welfare body calls for CADES report.

text.p: France's independent Social Security Accounts Commission on Monday called for published reports on the operations of welfare debt repayment fund (CADES) and complained that a supervisory board had not yet been set up.

In a report on welfare finances, it noted that a decree setting up CADES (Caisse d'Amortissement de la Dette Publique) earlier this year had allowed for a supervisory board including members of parliament and representatives of the welfare system.
"This supervisory board, whose membership was defined by article 4 of the decree of April 24, 1996, has not been set up to date," it said.
Neither had forecasts on CADES operations for 1996 and 1997 been given to the Social Security Accounts Commission as planned.

It noted that CADES had only recently been set up, but called for a report on CADES operations this year and next to be submitted at the same time as a government bill on welfare finances, to be debated by parliament next month.
The government said last week when it presented a budget for 1997 that CADES would show an accounting surplus next year.

This was due to the fact that CADES counted as revenue next year all the proceeds of a new tax, the RDS, which is meant to pay off the welfare debt, but counted as 1997 spending only interest payments rather than capital repayments on the debt.
The report estimated the revenue from the RDS (Remboursement de la Dette Sociale), a 0.5 percent tax on most income, at 21.5 billion francs this year and 25.5 billion next year.
